newsitem.title: GERMANY: ProSieben board member foresees boost from ads.
newsitem.headline: ProSieben board member foresees boost from ads.

text.p: Greeting the success of ProSieben AG's bourse debut, board member Michael Woelfle said on Monday he expected the company's television channels to keep expanding in the German advertising market.

Woelfle said the group's largest station, ProSieben, had long-term growth potential of 20 percent from advertising and the company's number two station, Kabel 1 would likely develop its ad base at an even greater rate.

"Advertising customers are very interested in the connection between advertising-financed television and new media like online services, " Woelfe said following ProSieben AG's first float on Monday morning.

"Therein lies significant potential for the ProSieben AG as well," said Woelfle, who is also the chief executive of MediaGruppe Muenchen, a marketing and market research firm which counts ProSieben AG among its clients.
Shares in the network traded well above their initial public offering price of 72 marks after their launch, closing at 95 marks in Frankfurt bourse trade.

The ProSieben group makes more than 90 percent of its income with ad-financed television. Company chairman Georg Kofler said in Frankfurt that the 360 million marks in intial stock proceeds would go towards TV programming.
He distanced himself anew from plans to invest in pay TV, saying the costs and risks of applying for the right to participate were too great.

"At the moment ProSieben has the rights to free TV but not for pay TV," Kofler said. "I think we spoke about it too early, but after looking into it, we made our decision (not to invest in pay television)."
Pro Sieben AG in September of last year shelved plans to roll out a pay TV channel called Sieben plus.
